invariants: Flow.id matches ^[a-z0-9-]+/[a-z0-9-]+$ (product slug '/' flow slug), so every id is two lowercase path segments and no two flows share one

Flow.canonical_url == '/flows/' + Flow.id for every Flow; the '/' inside the id stays a literal path separator and is never percent-encoded, so /flows/leafcutter/flow-render-pipeline is the link for leafcutter/flow-render-pipeline

The Flow records list every flow the Flows view can draw: the 27 stored flows in docs/product-truth/flows/ plus the Artifact Knowledge Graph (leafcutter/artifact-knowledge-graph, an architecture map of nodes with no steps, filed under Leafcutter by its id). None is a default entry any more: the bare /flows address shows the finder overview instead of a flow (v4, changing UXP-591-1-i)
Every Flow.drills_into[].flow resolves to a Flow.id, and Flow.drills_into[].step names the step of that Flow whose drill affordance opens it

Flow.product == the first segment of Flow.id and Flow.product_label is its display name (leafcutter -> 'Leafcutter', fern-and-fig -> 'Fern & Fig'); Flow.page_title == Flow.name + ' · Flows · Leafcutter Atlas'

Flow.actor_mix counts the flow's steps and branches by stored actor_kind, so actor_mix.deterministic + llm + human + jev == step_count + branch_count; Flow.io_gap_nodes counts those whose io_contracts declare missing_bindings; Flow.entities == the declared entities plus every entity a step or branch reads or writes, sorted by name; Flow.screens lists each screen a step or branch renders once, sorted by id, with its mockup's title

FlowRoute.resolution == 'finder' iff FlowRoute.requested_flow_id == null, i.e. the path is exactly /flows, with or without a finder query string; such a route draws no flow: rendered_flow == null, crumbs == [], open_drawer == null, filters == null, notice == null, step_notice == null, redirect_to == null, http_status 200, address_bar == requested_url (no redirect and no rewrite), and finder_query names the FlowFinderQuery whose url == requested_url (finder-overview for the bare /flows)

FlowRoute.resolution == 'selected' iff FlowRoute.requested_flow_id resolves to a Flow.id; then rendered_flow == requested_flow_id, address_bar == that Flow.canonical_url followed by '?step=' + requested_step when requested_step != null, http_status == 200 (a legacy link answers 308 instead, see redirect_to), and filters == {source: Flow.source, kind: Flow.kind, realization: all} so the flow selector lists the linked flow instead of falling back to the first flow of today's filters

FlowRoute.resolution == 'not-found' iff FlowRoute.requested_flow_id != null and resolves to no Flow.id; then rendered_flow == null and crumbs == [] (the view never silently renders any other flow or the finder), http_status == 404, address_bar == requested_url (the bad link stays visible so it can be corrected), and notice != null
FlowRoute.notice != null iff FlowRoute.resolution == 'not-found'; notice.detail quotes requested_flow_id verbatim and notice.action_href == '/flows'

FlowRoute.crumbs == [rendered_flow] whenever rendered_flow != null: a canonical URL names one flow, not the drill path it was reached by, so a freshly opened link shows that flow as the entry with no parent trail
FlowRoute.entered_via == 'ac-detail-link' iff FlowRoute.link_source != null; link_source resolves to a FlowAppearance.id and requested_url == that FlowAppearance.href

FlowRoute.requested_step == the ?step= value of requested_url, verbatim (for a legacy link, its &step= value); null when requested_url names no step. requested_flow_id never includes the query: it is the path after '/flows/' (for a legacy link, the percent-decoded ?flow= value)

A ?step= value (FlowRoute.requested_step, FlowAppearance.node_id) is looked up among the steps AND branches of its flow: within one flow, step ids and branch ids never collide (the explorer keys both as step:<id>), and a branch opens the same drawer a step does

FlowRoute.open_drawer != null iff rendered_flow != null and requested_step names a step or branch of rendered_flow; then open_drawer == requested_step: the page opens on that flow with that node's drawer open (one drawer at most)

FlowRoute.step_notice != null iff rendered_flow != null, requested_step != null and requested_step names no step or branch of rendered_flow; then open_drawer == null, the flow still renders as a selected route (http_status 200, crumbs == [rendered_flow], notice == null, the unknown ?step= stays in address_bar), step_notice.title == 'Step not found' and step_notice.detail quotes requested_step verbatim
FlowRoute.resolution == 'not-found' implies open_drawer == null and step_notice == null: a ?step= on an unknown flow id is not looked at, only the 'Flow not found' notice shows

FlowRoute.redirect_to != null iff requested_url is a legacy '/flows?flow=<id>&step=<step>' link (the form the AC drawer emitted before, the id's '/' percent-encoded as %2F); then redirect_to == '/flows/' + requested_flow_id + '?step=' + requested_step with the id's '/' literal, http_status == 308 (permanent redirect, so the legacy URL never stays in the tab's history), address_bar == redirect_to, and resolution, rendered_flow, crumbs, filters, open_drawer, notice and step_notice equal those of the FlowRoute whose requested_url == redirect_to (present in this dataset). redirect_to == null for every other route

A finder URL never carries a 'flow' or a 'step' parameter, so it is never taken for a legacy link (the 308 keys on 'flow' alone) and never opens a drawer; a flow's canonical address never carries finder state

FlowRoute.page_title == Flow.page_title of rendered_flow whenever a flow is drawn (also for a step link, an unknown ?step= and after a legacy redirect), 'Flows · Leafcutter Atlas' for the finder and 'Flow not found · Flows · Leafcutter Atlas' for an unknown flow id

FlowAppearance.href == the Flow.canonical_url of FlowAppearance.flow_id + '?step=' + FlowAppearance.node_id, for steps and branches alike, so following it opens that flow with that node's drawer open; it never uses the legacy /flows?flow=...&step=... form, and two appearances share an href only when they name the same node of the same flow
FlowAppearance.flow_name == the Flow.name of FlowAppearance.flow_id
FlowAppearance.node_id names a step (node_kind == 'step') or a branch (node_kind == 'branch') of flow_id whose implements[] contains FlowAppearance.ac, and node_label is that node's label
FlowAppearance.id == FlowAppearance.ac + '@' + FlowAppearance.flow_id + '#' + FlowAppearance.node_id

Within one FlowNavigation.session, seq starts at 1 and increases by 1; seq 1 is the only record with action == 'load' and history_op == 'initial', and its history_stack holds exactly one URL at history_index 0
FlowNavigation.address_bar == FlowNavigation.history_stack[FlowNavigation.history_index] for every record

FlowNavigation.history_op == 'push' iff action in {select, drill, crumb, open-result}: history_stack == the previous record's history_stack cut after its history_index, plus the new address_bar, and history_index == previous history_index + 1 (pushing drops any forward entries). select, drill and crumb land on the target Flow.canonical_url with no ?step= and drawer == null, also when a drawer was open (selecting or drilling from an open drawer closes it); open-result lands on the result's Flow.canonical_url from its flow card, or on the step row's href with that step's or branch's drawer open. The entry a push leaves keeps the URL last replaced into it

FlowNavigation.history_op == 'replace' iff action in {open-drawer, close-drawer, filter, search, facet}: history_stack == the previous record's history_stack with only the entry at history_index rewritten to the new address_bar (forward entries are kept, none is added) and history_index is unchanged, so opening, switching or closing a drawer, changing a filter, typing a search and ticking a facet never add a Back-button entry. open-drawer and close-drawer also keep rendered_flow, crumbs, shows and filters unchanged; a filter change keeps the flow and its URL (see the never-swap rule), so it rewrites the entry with the same URL and history_stack is unchanged

FlowNavigation.history_op == 'pop' iff action in {back, forward}: history_stack is unchanged, history_index moves by -1 (back) or +1 (forward), and address_bar, rendered_flow, crumbs, shows, drawer, filters, step_notice, finder_query, scope_notice and page_title equal those of the latest earlier record that wrote that history position (the load, a push, or a replace by open-drawer, close-drawer, filter, search or facet): Back and Forward move between flow and finder entries, an entry's drawer is whatever was last replaced into it, an entry a filter change rewrote comes back with that change's filters and notice, and a finder entry comes back with the search and facets last replaced into it

FlowNavigation.shows == 'graph' iff rendered_flow != null; then rendered_flow == the last of crumbs, finder_query == null and address_bar == that Flow.canonical_url, followed by '?step=' + drawer when drawer != null or by the unknown ?step= value that step_notice quotes when step_notice != null. shows == 'not-found' iff rendered_flow == null and address_bar names a flow id; then crumbs == [], drawer == null, step_notice == null, finder_query == null and scope_notice == null. shows == 'finder' iff the path of address_bar is exactly /flows; then rendered_flow == null, crumbs == [], drawer == null, step_notice == null, filters == null, scope_notice == null and finder_query names the FlowFinderQuery whose url == address_bar

FlowNavigation.drawer == the ?step= value of address_bar when that value names a step or branch of rendered_flow, and drawer == null when address_bar carries no ?step=: at most one drawer is open and the address bar always shares exactly what is on screen (a link whose ?step= names no step of the flow keeps that ?step= in address_bar with drawer == null and the 'Step not found' step_notice, as route-unknown-step and nav-clear-step-notice-1 show). The finder's address never carries ?step=, so drawer == null while it shows

FlowNavigation.action == 'open-drawer' implies drawer names a step or branch of rendered_flow, drawer != the previous record's drawer and address_bar == Flow.canonical_url of rendered_flow + '?step=' + drawer: opening a different step's drawer while one is open swaps the one ?step= value instead of adding a second. Enter on a focused step or branch card (key == 'Enter') does exactly what a click does, as nav-keyboard-step-drawer-2 shows

FlowNavigation.action == 'close-drawer' implies the previous record's drawer != null, drawer == null and address_bar == Flow.canonical_url of rendered_flow with no query. The drawer's close button has the accessible name 'Close step details', and Enter on it closes the drawer like a click (nav-keyboard-step-drawer-3)

FlowNavigation.action == 'drill' implies via_step != null, the previous record's rendered_flow has a drills_into entry {step: via_step, flow: rendered_flow}, and crumbs == previous crumbs + [rendered_flow]; via_step == null for every other action
FlowNavigation.action == 'select' implies crumbs == [rendered_flow]; action == 'crumb' implies crumbs is the previous crumbs cut after rendered_flow

No FlowNavigation record opens a drawer while the finder shows: owner ruling 1 of 2026-10-09 (a drawer opened on the bare /flows rewrote it to the default flow's step link) has nothing left to act on now that the bare /flows shows the finder, so every drawer opens on a flow's canonical URL

FlowNavigation.step_notice != null iff rendered_flow != null and address_bar carries a ?step= value that names no step or branch of rendered_flow; then drawer == null, step_notice.title == 'Step not found' and step_notice.detail quotes that value verbatim, equal to FlowRoute.step_notice for the same URL. Owner ruling 2 (2026-10-09): action == 'open-drawer' from such a state rewrites the unknown ?step= value to the opened step's or branch's id with history replace and clears step_notice, so the notice never outlives the unknown value and the unknown value never outlives the notice

FlowNavigation.filters == the {source, kind, realization} the Source / Kind / Realization controls of the flow page show after the action, and null while the finder shows. Seq 1 starts from the filters FlowRoute gives its URL (null for a finder URL; {source: real, kind: user, realization: all} for an unknown flow id; else {source: Flow.source, kind: Flow.kind, realization: all} of the linked flow); select, drill, crumb, open-drawer and close-drawer keep the previous record's filters, open-result sets those of the opened flow (as a fresh link to it would), back and forward restore them with their entry (see the pop rule), and otherwise only filter changes them

A filter change never swaps the drawn flow (v4, replacing owner ruling 3 of 2026-10-09, under which a filter change that excluded the entry flow re-picked another one): FlowNavigation.action == 'filter' (a click on a Source, Kind or Realization option) implies the previous record shows 'graph', filters != the previous record's filters, history_op == 'replace', and rendered_flow, crumbs, drawer, step_notice and address_bar equal the previous record's, ?step= included, so the entry is rewritten with the same URL. FlowNavigation.scope_notice != null iff shows == 'graph' and the entry flow crumbs[0] does not match filters (Flow.source != source, Flow.kind != kind, or realization not in {all, Flow.realization}); then scope_notice.title == 'Outside the current filters', scope_notice.detail names that flow and the three filter labels, and the flow stays drawn until the person picks another one

FlowNavigation.page_title == Flow.page_title of rendered_flow while shows == 'graph', 'Flows · Leafcutter Atlas' while shows == 'finder' and 'Flow not found · Flows · Leafcutter Atlas' while shows == 'not-found', equal to FlowRoute.page_title for the same URL; it changes with each push, replace and pop that changes what is shown

FlowNavigation.key == 'Enter' only on an open-drawer, close-drawer or open-result record done from the keyboard, and such a record equals what the matching click gives; key == null on every other record

FlowNavigation.action in {search, facet} implies the previous record shows 'finder' and this one does too, with address_bar == the new FlowFinderQuery.url, finder_query == that query and history_op == 'replace', so typing and ticking facets never add a Back entry. action == 'open-result' implies the previous record shows 'finder'; it pushes the result's address, crumbs == [the opened flow] and filters == {source: Flow.source, kind: Flow.kind, realization: all} of that flow, as a fresh link to it would give, and Back returns to the finder exactly as it was left (same URL, search, facets and results)

FlowNode.id == flow_id + '#' + node_id; node_id names a step (node_kind 'step', order its 1-based step order) or a branch (node_kind 'branch', order null) of flow_id, and label, text (the stored description), condition (a branch's condition; null for a step), actor_kind, agent, screen, entities (what it reads, then what it writes, each once), uses, produces and missing_io mirror that stored node

FlowNode.actor_label is the badge text for actor_kind: deterministic -> 'Code', llm -> 'AI agent', human -> 'Person', jev -> 'Jev' (Jev is its own value, never folded into AI agent); every step and branch card shows it as its actor badge, and the finder's step rows and Actor facet use the same words

FlowNode.uses / produces list, once each and in stored order, every field the node's io_contracts consume / produce as a field key: <contract>.<JSON-pointer segments joined by '.'> (just <contract> for the whole value), e.g. decision_record.selected_option_id. A field key's label is the contract's title (underscores and hyphens as spaces, first letter capitalised) + ' › ' + the segments joined by ' › ' ('Whole value' for the root), e.g. 'Decision record › selected_option_id', as the drawer's Inputs and Outputs tables show it

FlowNode.io_gap == true iff the node's io_contracts declare missing_bindings, and FlowNode.missing_io lists them ({name, direction} as stored, in stored order; [] iff io_gap is false). Such a node names few or none of the fields it really uses or produces, so a field search or a Uses / Produces field facet can miss it; the finder's 'I/O not yet defined' option (?io=gap) is how it is found. On 2026-10-13 that is 102 of the 306 stored steps and branches (62 steps, 40 branches) in 9 flows

FlowNode.href == Flow.canonical_url of flow_id + '?step=' + node_id. FlowNode.card_label == 'Step <order> of <Flow.step_count>: <label> (<actor_label>)' for a step and 'Branch: <label> (<actor_label>)' for a branch: the accessible name of its card, which is focusable and opens its drawer with Enter

FlowNode.ac_chips holds one chip per id in the node's implements[], in stored order: { ac, title == that AC's title, href == '/atlas?ac=' + ac }; following href opens the Atlas with that AC selected and its detail open, instead of today's component overview that ignores ?ac=

FlowNode holds every step and branch of leafcutter/decision-retrieval, leafcutter/deliver-a-feature, leafcutter/flow-render-pipeline and leafcutter/retrieval-query-build, so those flow pages can be drawn card by card; together they show all four actor badges, branches, a screen, AC chips and nodes with and without I/O gaps

FlowFinderQuery.url is the canonical finder address: '/flows', then '?' and the parameters when there are any: q first (form-encoded, spaces as '+'), then one parameter per chosen value, facets in the order product, actor, kind, realization, level, uses, produces, io, entity, screen, and values in their facet's option order (field keys sorted). Values are the stored ones (product slug, actor_kind, kind, realization, level, field key, gap, entity name, screen id), never labels, so a link stays valid when a label changes

Search (FlowFinderQuery.q) is case-insensitive: q and each target are split into words at every character that is not a letter or a digit (so snake_case, kebab-case, dotted field keys and AC ids split), and a target matches when every word of q starts some word of that ONE target. A step's or branch's targets are its label, each AC id, each produced field key, each used field key, its screen id with its title, each entity it reads or writes, and its text with its condition; a flow's own targets are its name with its id, and each entity it declares

Facets combine with OR within a facet and AND across facets. product, kind, realization, level and entity are flow facets (entity matches Flow.entities); actor, uses, produces, io and screen are step facets, which one step or branch must meet all at once; a node meets io=gap iff FlowNode.io_gap. A flow is listed iff it meets every flow facet and either nothing else is asked (no q and no step facet), or at least one of its steps or branches meets every step facet and q, or q matches the flow's own targets and (no step facet is chosen or one of its nodes meets them all). Its matching steps are the nodes that meet every step facet and q; with neither, it has none

Without q, FlowFinderQuery.results are ordered by product (Leafcutter, then Fern & Fig) and then by flow name, case-insensitive; with q, flows whose own targets match come first, then flows with more matching steps, then by name. flow_match == 'Name' or 'Entity · <name>' when q matches the flow's own targets, else null. Each result shows at most three step rows (steps in step order, then branches in stored order), more_steps == matching_steps - len(step_rows), and a row's href is that node's step link (<Flow.canonical_url>?step=<node_id>)

A step row's reason names the highest-ranked target q matched: 'Step label' or 'Branch label', 'AC <id>', 'Output · <field label>', 'Input · <field label>', 'Screen · <title>', 'Entity · <name>', then 'Text'. Without q it names the chosen step facet the node meets, first of produces ('Output · <field label>'), uses ('Input · <field label>'), io ('I/O not yet defined'), screen ('Screen · <title>') and actor ('<actor label>')

FlowFinderQuery.result_count.flows == len(results) and result_count.steps == the sum of matching_steps. facet_counts[f][v] == the number of flows the finder would list if v alone were chosen in facet f, with q and every other facet kept. Every option stays listed, 0 included (shown disabled, so the panel never jumps); entity options are sorted by name and screen options by title; uses and produces list only the chosen fields, since they are picked by type-ahead; io always lists its one option, gap. With no q and no facet, the counts follow from the Flow records alone: product, kind, realization and level count Flow fields, actor v counts flows with actor_mix[v] > 0, io gap counts flows with io_gap_nodes > 0, entity counts Flow.entities and screen counts Flow.screens

FlowFinderQuery.status_text, which a polite live region announces, is '<n> flows' with no q and no facet, 'No flows match' when nothing is listed, '<F> flow(s), <S> step(s) match' when q or a step facet is chosen, and '<F> flow(s) match' otherwise

FlowFinderQuery.applied_chips holds one chip per chosen facet value, in URL order, labelled '<facet label>: <option label>' (facet labels Product, Actor, Kind, Realization, Level, Uses field, Produces field, I/O, Entity, Screen; option labels Flow.product_label, FlowNode.actor_label, User / Data / Architecture, Built / Spec / Sample, Journey / Pipeline / Agent, the field label, 'I/O not yet defined', the entity name, the screen title); the io facet has one option, so its chip is labelled 'I/O not yet defined' alone, never 'I/O: I/O not yet defined'; remove_href == url without that one value, and the chip's remove button is named 'Remove filter ' + its label. clear_all_href == url with every facet removed and q kept, null when no facet is chosen

FlowFinderQuery.empty_state != null iff results == []; then its title is "No flows match '<q>'" ('No flows match these filters' without q) and it holds one suggestion per applied chip: { label: 'Remove ' + the chip's label, href: its remove_href, flows: how many flows that address lists }

Every FlowFinderQuery is shown by a FlowRoute (finder_query) or a FlowNavigation record. Its results and counts were measured on 2026-10-12 against the 27 stored flows (200 steps and 106 branches) plus the Artifact Knowledge Graph, as the Flow records mirror them; the io facet's results and counts were measured on 2026-10-13 against the same store

The 'I/O not yet defined' option finds every gap: /flows?io=gap (finder-io-gap) lists exactly the flows with Flow.io_gap_nodes > 0, each with matching_steps == its io_gap_nodes, so result_count.steps == the sum of Flow.io_gap_nodes (102 nodes in 9 flows), and the overview's facet_counts.io.gap == that flow count (9). Like every option it counts flows; the result summary gives the steps

fields.id: string — the flow's path-stable id, <product>/<name> (product-truth artifact id)
fields.name: string — the flow's display name (the selector button label, the page heading and the finder's result card title)
fields.kind: enum: user | data | architecture — drives the Kind filter
fields.source: enum: real | mock — drives the Source filter
fields.realization: enum: built | spec | mock — drives the Realization filter and the realization banner
fields.level: enum: journey | pipeline | agent — the level chip (journey → pipeline → agent = drill deeper)
fields.canonical_url: string — '/flows/' + id; the one shareable address of this flow
fields.drills_into: array of { step, flow } — each step whose drill affordance opens a sub-flow, and that sub-flow's Flow.id (first expands_to target)
fields.product: enum: leafcutter | fern-and-fig — the product slug, the first segment of id; the Product facet's value (?product= in a finder URL)
fields.product_label: string — the product's display name (Leafcutter | Fern & Fig), the Product facet's option label
fields.page_title: string — the document <title> while the flow is drawn: '<name> · Flows · Leafcutter Atlas', so tabs and history entries can be told apart
fields.step_count: integer — the flow's steps (0 for the Artifact Knowledge Graph, a map of nodes rather than steps)
fields.branch_count: integer — the flow's branches (its 'what if' paths)
fields.actor_mix: object { deterministic, llm, human, jev } — how many of the flow's steps and branches each actor kind runs (stored actor_kind); the finder's result card shows it as Code · AI agent · Person · Jev counts
fields.io_gap_nodes: integer — the flow's steps and branches whose io_contracts declare missing_bindings (an input or output not yet bound to a field), which a field search can miss; the finder's 'I/O not yet defined' option (?io=gap) lists the flow with that many matching steps
fields.entities: array of entity names — the flow's declared entities plus every entity one of its steps or branches reads or writes; the Entity facet matches these
fields.screens: array of { screen, title } — each screen (mockup) one of its steps or branches renders, once, with the mockup's title; the Screen facet matches these

fields.id: string — fixture handle for this address
fields.requested_url: string — the URL as typed, pasted, bookmarked or followed, query included
fields.requested_flow_id: string | null — the flow id the URL names: everything after '/flows/' in the path, verbatim and without the query; for a legacy /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> link, the percent-decoded ?flow= value; null for /flows, with or without a finder query
fields.requested_step: string | null — the ?step= value (for a legacy link, its &step= value), verbatim: the step or branch whose drawer the link asks to open; null when the URL names no step
fields.entered_via: enum: nav-link | address-bar | shared-link | ac-detail-link — nav-link == the sidebar 'Flows' link; address-bar == typed or bookmarked; shared-link == opened from outside the Atlas (chat, ticket, PR); ac-detail-link == an 'Appears in flows' link in the AC detail drawer
fields.link_source: string | null — FlowAppearance.id of the drawer link that was followed; null unless entered_via == ac-detail-link
fields.resolution: enum: finder | selected | not-found — finder == the bare /flows address, with or without a finder query string: it shows the finder (search box, facets, results grouped by flow) and draws no flow
fields.redirect_to: string | null — for a legacy /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> link, the step link it redirects to (/flows/<id>?step=<step>); null for every other URL
fields.rendered_flow: string | null — Flow.id drawn on the canvas; null for not-found and for the finder
fields.crumbs: array of Flow.id — the breadcrumb trail right after the page opens; [] for not-found and for the finder

fields.session: string — one browser tab's walk through the Flows view
fields.seq: integer — 1-based order of the action within the session
fields.action: enum: load | select | drill | crumb | open-drawer | close-drawer | filter | search | facet | open-result | back | forward — load == the page opens; select == a flow-selector button; drill == a step's drill affordance (on the node, or the 'Open sub-flow' button in its drawer); crumb == a breadcrumb; open-drawer == a click on a step or branch, or Enter on its focused card, which opens its drawer or swaps the open drawer for it; close-drawer == the drawer's close button (named 'Close step details'; a click or Enter) or a click on the canvas beside the drawer; filter == a click on a Source, Kind or Realization filter option on a flow page; search == typing in the finder's search box (the record is the state once typing settles); facet == a click on a finder facet option, an applied-filter chip's remove button or 'Clear all'; open-result == a click (or Enter) on a finder result: its flow card opens the flow, a step row opens the flow at that step; back / forward == the browser buttons
fields.trigger: string — what the person did, in words
fields.via_step: string | null — the step whose drill affordance was clicked; null unless action == drill
fields.history_op: enum: initial | push | replace | pop — what the action does to the tab's history; replace rewrites the current entry in place and adds none (a filter change rewrites it with the same URL; typing and facet clicks rewrite the finder entry with the new finder URL)
fields.history_stack: array of URLs — the tab's Flows-view history entries after the action
fields.history_index: integer — 0-based position of the current entry in history_stack
fields.address_bar: string — the URL shown after the action (== history_stack[history_index]); <Flow.canonical_url>?step=<drawer> while a drawer is open; the finder URL (FlowFinderQuery.url) while the finder shows
fields.rendered_flow: string | null — Flow.id drawn on the canvas; null when the not-found state or the finder shows
fields.crumbs: array of Flow.id — the breadcrumb trail after the action, entry flow first; [] while the not-found state or the finder shows
fields.drawer: string | null — the step or branch id whose drawer is open after the action (one at most), equal to the ?step= value of address_bar; null when no drawer is open
fields.filters: object | null — the Source / Kind / Realization filter state of the flow page after the action; it travels with the history entry like the breadcrumb trail, so Back and Forward restore it; null while the finder shows
fields.step_notice: object | null — the 'Step not found' notice { title, detail } shown over rendered_flow while address_bar carries a ?step= that names no step or branch of it (as FlowRoute.step_notice); null otherwise
fields.finder_query: string | null — FlowFinderQuery.id of the finder state on screen after the action; null unless shows == finder
fields.scope_notice: object | null — the 'Outside the current filters' notice { title, detail } shown over the drawn flow while its entry flow (crumbs[0]) does not match the filters; a filter change never swaps the drawn flow, it raises this notice instead; null otherwise
fields.page_title: string — the document <title> after the action (as FlowRoute.page_title), updated on every push, replace and pop that changes what is shown
fields.key: string | null — 'Enter' when the person did the action from the keyboard (Enter on a focused step card, the drawer's close button or a finder result); null for a click, a typed or followed URL, or a browser button

fields.flow_id: string — Flow.id the step or branch belongs to
fields.node_id: string — the step or branch id (the ?step= value of its step link)
fields.order: integer | null — the step's 1-based order; null for a branch
fields.label: string — the card title, searched with high weight
fields.text: string — the plain-language description, searched as text
fields.condition: string | null — a branch's 'what if' condition, searched as text; null for a step
fields.actor_kind: enum: deterministic | llm | human | jev — the stored mechanism that runs it; the Actor facet's value (?actor= in a finder URL)
fields.actor_label: enum: Code | AI agent | Person | Jev — the actor badge every step card shows, and the Actor facet's option label
fields.agent: string | null — the named actor as stored (free text, searched as text only)
fields.card_label: string — the accessible name of the step card, which is focusable and opens its drawer with Enter
fields.href: string — the step link <Flow.canonical_url>?step=<node_id>; a finder step row opens it
fields.screen: string | null — the screen (mockup) id the node renders; the Screen facet's value
fields.screen_title: string | null — that mockup's title, the Screen facet's option label
fields.entities: array of entity names — what the node reads or writes
fields.uses: array of field keys — every field its io_contracts consume (the Uses field facet's values, ?uses= in a finder URL)
fields.produces: array of field keys — every field its io_contracts produce (the Produces field facet's values, ?produces=)
fields.io_gap: boolean — true when its io_contracts declare missing_bindings, so some of its inputs or outputs are not named fields yet; the finder's 'I/O not yet defined' option (?io=gap) matches exactly these nodes
fields.missing_io: array of { name, direction } — each binding its io_contracts declare missing (missing_bindings, in stored order): name as stored, direction consumes | produces | both (Input | Output | Input and output); [] when io_gap is false. The drawer shows each as a 'Proposed — missing JSON binding' section
fields.ac_chips: array of { ac, title, href } — the acceptance-criteria chips in its drawer; href == '/atlas?ac=<ac>' opens that AC in the Atlas

records.label: Look up matching records
records.text: The kernel searches the decision index for earlier records that match the new decision's components and roadmap phase, scores them by text and checks each file is unchanged.
records.card_label: Step 1 of 5: Look up matching records (Code)

ac_chips.title: A new decision looks up earlier published decisions through the index

records.label: Ask Jev whether each applies
records.text: Jev judges, for up to three candidate records, whether each earlier decision applies here, asking once before options exist and then alongside the option assessment.
records.card_label: Step 2 of 5: Ask Jev whether each applies (Jev)

ac_chips.title: Earlier decisions are judged for fit, and those that apply are cited with their approver

records.label: Cite it as evidence
records.text: The kernel turns a precedent scoring 0.5 or more into evidence that cites the earlier record and who approved it.
records.card_label: Step 3 of 5: Cite it as evidence (Code)

ac_chips.title: Earlier decisions are judged for fit, and those that apply are cited with their approver

records.label: Reuse it, or decide anew?
records.text: When a precedent scores 0.8 or more, is not superseded and the decision has no options of its own, you are asked whether to reuse it or decide anew.
records.card_label: Step 4 of 5: Reuse it, or decide anew? (Person)

ac_chips.title: A close match asks you once: reuse it, or decide anew?

records.label: Reuse the earlier choice
records.text: The kernel resolves the decision with the earlier choice, approved by you, and stages a new record that cites the precedent.
records.card_label: Step 5 of 5: Reuse the earlier choice (Code)

ac_chips.title: Reusing an earlier decision is your fresh approval, staged as a new record

records.label: Does not apply
records.text: The kernel leaves the earlier decision out, and the new decision carries on without it.
records.card_label: Branch: Does not apply (Code)

ac_chips.title: An earlier decision scored below the applies threshold is left out

records.label: Evidence only, no reuse question
records.text: The kernel keeps the precedent as cited evidence and the normal forming flow continues without interrupting you.
records.condition: the score is below 0.8, the new decision already has options, or the precedent is superseded
records.card_label: Branch: Evidence only, no reuse question (Code)

ac_chips.title: An applicable precedent below the reuse threshold is cited without a reuse question
A superseded precedent is cited but never offered for reuse
A decision that already has options of its own gets no reuse question

records.label: Decide anew
records.text: The normal forming flow continues with the precedent kept as evidence, and if you end up choosing differently the new record supersedes the old one.
records.card_label: Branch: Decide anew (Person)

ac_chips.title: Deciding anew keeps the precedent as evidence and supersedes it only if you choose differently

records.label: Plan
records.text: You say what you want and AI agents author the acceptance criteria for it.
records.card_label: Step 1 of 3: Plan (AI agent)

ac_chips.title: New requirements flow into the AC store through a single command

records.label: Build
records.text: AI phase agents drive the wired ticket through its build phases until it is green and committed.
records.card_label: Step 2 of 3: Build (AI agent)

ac_chips.title: Workflow scripts orchestrate agents deterministically — no silent skips, no stale state

records.label: Finalize
records.text: The finalize pipeline merges the pull request and closes the epic or ticket.
records.card_label: Step 3 of 3: Finalize (Code)

ac_chips.title: Integration failures are caught before code reaches main

records.label: Read and normalize the stored flow JSON
records.text: Atlas reads every stored flow, turns each readable one into the shape its views draw, and adds the artifact knowledge graph as an architecture view.
records.card_label: Step 1 of 3: Read and normalize the stored flow JSON (Code)

ac_chips.title: The /flows loader reads the flow and index JSON from the product-truth store
The loader discovers every flow file in the store rather than a hardcoded list

records.label: Resolve each step to its AC's live work_status
records.text: Atlas gives each step and branch the live work status of its linked acceptance criteria, keeping the stored status for unknown criteria and never changing the criteria.
records.card_label: Step 2 of 3: Resolve each step to its AC's live work_status (Code)

ac_chips.title: Each flow step resolves to its acceptance criterion's live work_status
A step whose acceptance-criteria id does not resolve renders as an unknown/fallback status

records.label: Draw the graph on the /flows page
records.text: Atlas passes the flows, their mock records and screen titles to the Flows page, which draws each flow as a graph and shows each step's inputs and outputs in its drawer.
records.card_label: Step 3 of 3: Draw the graph on the /flows page (Code)

ac_chips.title: The resolved flow is drawn as a graph on the Atlas /flows page
Each rendered step is colour-coded by its resolved work_status

records.label: Decide whether a query is missing
records.text: Jev chooses to build a new query only when the source data is supported and none of the offered queries fits, without writing the request itself.
records.card_label: Step 1 of 5: Decide whether a query is missing (Jev)

records.label: Construct the scoped request
records.text: The system assembles the original need, the input and output requirements and the source-fit evidence, skips duplicate builds and hands the request to the coding agent.
records.card_label: Step 2 of 5: Construct the scoped request (Code)

records.label: Build a candidate query
records.text: The coding agent writes a parameterized, bounded query with its input and output contract, tests and evaluation cases, keeping the question and context for resuming.
records.card_label: Step 3 of 5: Build a candidate query (AI agent)

records.label: Verify and register
records.text: The system independently verifies the candidate query and registers a version only with the required permission, keeping failed candidates visible but unregistered.
records.card_label: Step 4 of 5: Verify and register (Code)

records.label: Resume the original need
records.text: The system runs the newly registered query for the waiting question and hands the result back for comparison, so later requests can reuse it.
records.card_label: Step 5 of 5: Resume the original need (Code)

records.label: Stop a rejected build
records.text: The system neither registers nor runs the rejected query, keeps its failure and the original need, and returns to method selection or reports a partial or blocked result.
records.card_label: Branch: Stop a rejected build (Code)

fields.id: string — fixture handle for this finder state
fields.url: string — the canonical /flows address of this state (the query string IS the finder state, so the address can be shared, bookmarked and reloaded)
fields.q: string | null — the search text as typed (trimmed); null when the search box is empty
fields.facets: object { product, actor, kind, realization, level, uses, produces, io, entity, screen } — the chosen values per facet (stored values, never labels); [] when none. io has one value, gap: the 'I/O not yet defined' option
fields.status_text: string — the result summary, also announced by a polite live region
fields.result_count: object { flows, steps } — flows listed and matching steps across them
fields.applied_chips: array of { facet, value, label, remove_href } — one removable chip per chosen facet value, shown above the results
fields.clear_all_href: string | null — the 'Clear all' link: url with every facet removed and q kept; null when no facet is chosen
fields.empty_state: object | null — { title, detail, suggestions[{ label, href, flows }] } when nothing matches: each suggestion removes one chosen filter and says how many flows that would list; null otherwise
fields.results: array of { flow_id, flow_name, href, flow_match, matching_steps, step_rows[{ node_id, node_kind, label, actor_kind, actor_label, reason, href }], more_steps } — results grouped by flow; a step row opens the flow at that step
fields.facet_counts: object facet -> { value: flows } — the count beside each facet option: how many flows the finder would list if that option alone were chosen in its facet

provenance.note: Created: no canonical dataset existed for Flow in ux-prototyping (by_entity.Flow.canonical_mock_data was empty; ux-prototyping's only dataset, fern-and-fig/catalog, models Plant/Customer/Order/Payment). THE canonical dataset for the Atlas /flows view and its canonical flow URLs (/flows/<flow id>). Flow records mirror twelve real flows in docs/product-truth/flows/ (names, kind, source, realization, level and expands_to drill targets as stored; leafcutter/deliver-a-feature is the DEFAULT_ENTRY in leafcutter-web/components/flows/flows-view.tsx). FlowRoute covers every way the view can be opened: the bare /flows default entry; shared, bookmarked and AC-drawer links to real/mock, journey/pipeline/agent and architecture flows (filters follow the linked flow); step links (/flows/<flow id>?step=<node id>) that open the flow with a step's or a branch's drawer open; a step id the flow does not have (the flow opens with no drawer and a 'Step not found' notice); four unknown flow ids (a typo, a product name alone, a step appended as a path segment, a typo carrying ?step=) that show a 404 not-found state instead of falling back; and a legacy /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> link (as the AC drawer emitted it, id percent-encoded) that redirects with 308 to the step link. FlowAppearance mirrors real AC-drawer 'Appears in flows' entries (one flow, two flows, three steps of one flow, and two branch appearances), each pointing at <canonical url>?step=<node id> instead of today's /flows?flow=...&step=... query that FlowsView ignores. FlowNavigation walks three browser sessions: drill-and-return (push, back, forward, breadcrumb push dropping the forward entry), a shared mock journey (drill, select, back twice) and recovering from an unknown id (back returns to the not-found state). Revised 2026-10-08 before the first commit, per the owner's mock-data-gate decision (approved with one edit to assumption 5): a step link is /flows/<flow id>?step=<stepId> and opens that flow with that step's drawer open; the AC drawer's 'Appears in flows' links use that form; old /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> links redirect to the new URL; a step id the flow does not have opens the flow without a drawer and says the step was not found. Branches use the same ?step= form because the explorer opens the same drawer for a branch as for a step (flow-step-view.ts keys both as step:<id>; no flow has a step and a branch with the same id). Assumptions 1-4 unchanged: bare /flows keeps its URL and shows the default flow; an unknown flow id answers 404 with a 'Flow not found' notice quoting the id, a link back to /flows and the selector, drawing no other flow; opening a flow link sets the Source and Kind filters to that flow's, Realization all; a fresh link shows only that flow in the breadcrumb and back/forward restore each entry's breadcrumb. Not modelled: a legacy ?flow= link without &step=. Extend this dataset; do not start a second Flow dataset.

Extended to v2 per the owner's decision at the mockup gate on 2026-10-09, verbatim: "Opening a step's drawer writes ?step=<id> into the address bar and closing it removes it, using history 'replace' (no new back-button entries) — the current URL always shares exactly what you see. Selecting or drilling to another flow still pushes a new entry." The owner also confirmed two details v1 already models: a legacy /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> link answers a permanent 308 redirect (route-legacy-step-link), and an unknown ?step= stays visible in the address bar (route-unknown-step). FlowNavigation gains a drawer field (the step or branch whose drawer is open, null when none; every v1 record has drawer null), two actions, open-drawer (a click on a step or branch, also to swap one open drawer for another) and close-drawer (the drawer's X button or a click beside it), and the history_op replace, which rewrites the current entry in place, keeps forward entries and adds none. Select, drill and crumb still push, always to the target flow's canonical URL with no ?step=. Three sessions show it: drawer-replace (open a flow, open the 'Plan' drawer, switch to 'Build', close it, drill into the build pipeline; one Back press returns to the flow with no drawer, because the three drawer actions added no entries); drawer-in-history (a step link from an AC drawer opens with the drawer, the drawer's 'Open sub-flow' button pushes the sub-flow with no ?step=, Back reopens the drawer because that entry still carries ?step=code, closing it replaces the entry, and after Forward then Back the flow returns with no drawer); select-from-open-drawer (picking another flow in the selector while a drawer is open pushes that flow's URL with no ?step=, and Back restores the drawer). New invariants cover replace, open-drawer, close-drawer and drawer == ?step=; the push, pop and graph invariants now include the drawer. Still not modelled: a legacy ?flow= link without &step=. Today's drawer lays a scrim over the canvas that closes it on click, so switching straight from one drawer to another (nav-drawer-replace-3) needs the click to reach the other step.

Extended to v3 per the owner's three rulings at the flow gate on 2026-10-09, verbatim intent: "Approve with three rulings that keep the URL always matching the screen: 1. Opening a drawer while on bare /flows replaces the URL with the default flow's canonical URL plus ?step=<id>. 2. Opening a real step's drawer after a "Step not found" notice clears the notice and replaces the unknown ?step= value. 3. When a Source, Kind or Realization filter change makes a different flow render, the URL is replaced (no new Back entry) with that flow's canonical URL." FlowNavigation gains two fields on every record: filters (the Source / Kind / Realization state the controls show; no earlier session changes a filter, so each earlier record keeps the filters its session opened with) and step_notice (the 'Step not found' notice while address_bar carries an unknown ?step=; null on every earlier record). It gains one action, filter (a click on a Source, Kind or Realization option), which always uses history replace. Three sessions show the rulings. drawer-on-bare-flows (ruling 1): on /flows, clicking 'Plan' replaces /flows with /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature?step=plan, and closing the drawer leaves /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature, not /flows. clear-step-notice (ruling 2): a link with ?step=lint opens python-coder-internal with the notice; clicking 'Doc-enforcer' replaces ?step=lint with ?step=docenforce and clears the notice; after selecting another flow, Back returns to the Doc-enforcer drawer, never to the unknown step. filter-replace (ruling 3): drilled into the build pipeline with the 'Coders make it green (prio 6-8)' drawer open, Realization 'Built' keeps the entry flow, so the URL, the trail and the drawer stay; Realization 'Spec' leaves only 'Define a feature the product-truth way' in scope, so it renders with a one-flow breadcrumb and no drawer and replaces /flows/leafcutter/how-acs-are-built?step=code in place; Back returns to the deliver-a-feature entry with its own filters, and Forward returns the define-a-feature entry as the filter change left it. Which flow a filter change renders is today's rule in flows-view.tsx: the entry flow stays while it matches the new filters, otherwise the first flow the selector lists under them. Assumption, not ruled by the owner: filters travel with each history entry the way the breadcrumb trail does, so Back and Forward restore an entry's filters (the entry's flow has to be listed by the selector, and the filters a fresh load would pick are the flow's own, which differ for a drilled sub-flow). The replace, pop, graph and drawer == ?step= invariants now cover the filter action, filters and step_notice; new invariants cover rulings 1 to 3, filters and step_notice. The three ruled items are removed from the not-modelled lists of the two entries above. Still not modelled: a legacy ?flow= link without &step=; a filter change while the 'Flow not found' notice shows.

Extended to v4 for the Atlas Flow finder (plan-feature request, ux-prototyping): bare /flows becomes a finder overview page instead of opening the default flow, which changes UXP-591-1-i. Flow now mirrors every flow the view can draw: the 12 v3 records plus the 15 other stored flows (decision, retrieval, criteria-library, ac-lifecycle, generate-product-truth) and the Artifact Knowledge Graph, 28 in all; it loses is_default_entry and gains product, product_label, page_title (the per-flow <title>), step_count, branch_count, actor_mix, io_gap_nodes, entities and screens, all measured from the stored flow files on 2026-10-12. New entity FlowNode: a step or branch as the finder indexes it and its card shows it (actor badge, focusable card name, AC chips that link to /atlas?ac=<id>, field keys it uses and produces, I/O gap), complete for decision-retrieval, deliver-a-feature, flow-render-pipeline and retrieval-query-build. New entity FlowFinderQuery: nine finder states with their canonical /flows?... address, search text, chosen facets (Product, Actor, Kind, Realization, Level, Uses field, Produces field, Entity, Screen), counts beside every option, applied-filter chips, results grouped by flow with up to three step rows that open /flows/<product>/<flow>?step=<id>, and the empty state. They were computed by running the matching rules in the invariants over the real store: the overview (28 flows; Code 23, AI agent 17, Person 12, Jev 8 flows), a text search 'selected option' (5 flows, 27 steps) and the same narrowed to Person (2 flows, 5 steps), Produces field and Uses field searches on decision_record.selected_option_id, a Jev search (Jev is its own Actor value), an AC-id prefix search (UXP-210d), an entity plus screen search (Order on Checkout) and a search with no results. FlowRoute: route-bare-flows now resolves to the finder (no flow, no breadcrumb, filters null); seven new finder routes show that a search is shareable and bookmarkable; every route gains finder_query and page_title. FlowNavigation: every record gains finder_query, scope_notice, page_title and key; shows gains 'finder' and action gains search, facet and open-result. New session find-and-open-step (open /flows, type, tick Person, open a step row, Back restores the same search) and keyboard-step-drawer (Enter opens a step's drawer, Enter on the drawer's 'Close step details' button closes it). Quick win 'changing a filter never swaps the drawn flow' replaces owner ruling 3: filter-replace seq 5 now keeps the flow, its trail, its drawer and its URL and shows an 'Outside the current filters' notice, and Forward (seq 7) returns that state. drill-and-return now starts from a bookmarked link to 'Deliver a feature end-to-end' instead of the bare /flows. The drawer-on-bare-flows session (owner ruling 1) is removed: the bare /flows no longer draws a flow, so no drawer can open on it. Assumptions, not ruled by the owner: facet counts count flows; entity is a flow facet while actor, uses, produces and screen must be met by one and the same step; field facets use dotted field keys (contract.path) and repeat the parameter for several values so URLSearchParams leaves them readable; the Artifact Knowledge Graph stays in the finder under Leafcutter (it has no product); the flow page keeps its Source / Kind / Realization filters, which stay in history.state, never in the address. Not modelled: the type-ahead suggestion list of the field facets, keyboard movement through results, the graph highlight lens, a 'Steps list' view, unknown finder parameter values, and a legacy ?flow= link without &step=. The explore-flows-in-atlas record mirrors that flow as stored before this feature's flow-author pass; when finder steps are added its counts, entities and screens need a refresh. Revised 2026-10-13 before the first commit of v4, per the owner's mock-data-gate decision (approved with one addition): add an 'I/O not yet defined' filter value so the 102 steps whose input or output fields are not filled in yet can be found in the finder. The finder gains a one-option step facet io (value gap, label 'I/O not yet defined', facet label 'I/O', URL position after produces: /flows?io=gap); a node meets it iff FlowNode.io_gap, a step row it alone selects gives the reason 'I/O not yet defined', and its chip carries the option label alone. Every FlowFinderQuery gains facets.io and facet_counts.io (the overview counts 9 flows; the existing results and counts are unchanged). Two new finder states: finder-io-gap (9 flows, 102 steps: 62 steps and 40 branches) and finder-io-gap-ai-agent (with Actor 'AI agent': 6 flows, 8 steps). FlowRoute route-bookmarked-finder-io-gap opens that list from a bookmark and route-shared-finder-io-gap-ai-agent the narrowed list from a shared link, whose 'Build a candidate query' row opens /flows/leafcutter/retrieval-query-build?step=author. No new FlowNavigation session: that entity is at its 50-record bound, and find-and-open-step already shows ticking a facet, opening a step row and Back returning to the same list. FlowNode gains missing_io (each missing binding's name and direction as stored), so an opened step shows what is still undefined. Assumptions, not ruled by the owner: the option's count counts flows like every other option (the result summary says '9 flows, 102 steps match'); there is no complementary 'I/O defined' option; with produces, uses and io chosen together a row's reason names the field first. Not modelled: searching the text of a missing binding's name or reason.
